text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Conservative coalition party leader Tansu Ciller orders her party ministers to start implementing National Security Council decisions aimed at quelling Islamist activism.
- A former armed forces chief, now a conservative government MP, begins talks with other parties on the possibility of forming an alternative coalition.
- The crowd at the final of the Prime Minister's Cup soccer match chant pro-secularist slogans and boo the arrival of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
- An Islamist militant training centre is discovered in Gebze, a town close to Istanbul.
- A parliamentary commission investigating apparent links between state officials and underworld gangs backs down on questioning Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller and her husband.
- The Turkish military kills 49 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels in a six-day operation near the Iraqi border.
- Economy technocrats are concerned that the strengthening of the dollar in international currency markets will have an impact on the Turkish economy.
- A former special forces chief gives himself up to the State Security Court where he faces charges of links to a security scandal.
